title: Address "confirmation" by dialling a code vs. agent confirms the address verbally
summary: A SwiftShip Couriers caller phones about a ShopKart parcel that is out for delivery and says the address is hard to locate. In the legitimate case, the agent asks for a landmark and whether someone is home, and says they will call on reaching the gate. In the fraud case, the caller says the address must be "confirmed" by dialling a short code followed by a phone number the caller reads out; this kind of code can switch on call forwarding so the recipient's calls, including voice OTPs, reach the caller. The catalog originally described this family as "link to update address and pay". It was changed to a dial-code request because the link-and-fee mechanism is already covered by `ec_03`. Both callers use the words "confirm your address" and "your number".

shared_setting.recipient_profile: a ShopKart customer at home or at work; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: The parcel is prepaid, worth [AMOUNT_24] (₹500–₹8,000), and out for delivery today.
Both callers give an agent name, the order, and say they are in the recipient's area.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller asks the recipient to dial a network code followed by a phone number to "confirm" an address. Address confirmation needs no dialling; such codes can divert the recipient's incoming calls to the caller.
fraud.caller_objective: Activate call forwarding to intercept verification calls and voice OTPs.
stable_facts: The caller says the "system" needs the recipient's number "linked" to the delivery.
The code is described only as a short code starting with a symbol, followed by a 10-digit number [PHONE_2]; the actual code is never emitted.
The caller does not ask for a landmark.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may repeat the code, say the parcel will be returned, or claim it is a new "security step". They must not switch to links, payments, OTP requests, or app installation. The legitimate agent must not ask the recipient to dial, install, pay, or share any code.

must_preserve: confirm your address" and "your number" in both cases
verbal landmark and call on arrival in _L
must_not_emit: any real USSD or network code
narrator explanations of what the code does

ambiguities: A caller mentioning "your number" or "the system" is not evidence; the legitimate agent also refers to calling the recipient's number.
If generation writes a real network code, the prefix must be rejected for safety.
The legitimate half resembles ec_03_L (verbal address confirmation); the fraud halves differ clearly (dial code vs. paid link).

evidence_references.claim: Callers have tricked mobile users into dialling codes that activate call forwarding; DoT suspended USSD call forwarding from April 2024 (CE19)
Courier impersonators have asked recipients to dial codes to "confirm" or "unlock" delivery (CE20)
Real courier agents never ask recipients to dial network codes
